battle.name: 大哥倫比亞-秘魯戰爭
battle.theater: 厄瓜多爾山區與秘魯北部高原
battle.brief: 一八二八年秘魯在北線向大哥倫比亞挑戰，波利瓦爾於塔爾基取勝後越境深入，卻在 Ingaví 一役失利；蘇克雷同年奪下亞亞庫喬，次年再克利馬，戰事以瓜亞基爾協議收束。卡面輪發手槍是十六世紀西班牙火槍隊軍官的制式自衛武器，到一八二八年早已讓位給燧發手槍。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 交戰一方是大哥倫比亞共和國，名義上由委內瑞拉、新格拉納達與基多（即厄瓜多爾）三個省組成，首都波哥大，一八二八年全國常備軍約三萬五千至四萬人，另有各省民兵與基多工匠組成的志願兵大隊。軍隊以拿破崙式編制為骨幹：步兵營由四個連的輕步兵加一個近衛連組成，槍兵居中、擲彈兵與獵兵分列兩翼，炮兵連以四磅與六磅炮為主，另有輕騎兵、長槍騎兵與帶卡賓槍的槍騎兵。指揮系統上，波利瓦爾以最高統帥身分直接統率解放軍，蘇克雷自一八二七年起出任基多省長兼該區軍政總督，亞亞庫喬之後升任元帥並受封大元帥，海軍則由駐瓜亞基爾分隊的托馬斯·查爾斯率領。對手是秘魯共和國，一八二一年脫離西班牙統治，首都利馬，國力與財政都遠弱於對方。一八二七年一月總統拉瓦·阿吉羅被軍方推翻並流放歐洲，秘魯此後由立法機關與最高軍事委員會共同主持；一八二八年六月召開制憲會議，另組北方軍交由何塞·德·拉·馬爾全權統帥，海軍由海軍上將馬丁率領分隊，皇家派殘部則由佩蘇埃拉以大元帥之名率領並歸順政府。一八二九年六月拉馬爾推翻中央政府，在南部另立秘魯大元帥政府，與利馬的加馬拉政府分裂作戰，使這場戰爭演成三方互相消耗的持久戰。
countriesEn: One side was the Republic of Gran Colombia, nominally a federation of Venezuela, New Granada and the Quito department, in effect Ecuador, with its capital at Bogota. Its standing army numbered roughly 35,000 to 40,000 men in 1828, supplemented by provincial militias and volunteer companies drawn from the guilds of Quito. The army was built on the Napoleonic model: infantry battalions of four line companies with a grenadier company, musketeers in the centre and light troops on the flanks, artillery batteries around 4- and 6-pound guns, plus light cavalry, lancers and mounted skirmishers with carbines. On the command side, Simon Bolivar led the Libertadores as commander-in-chief; Sucre governed the Quito department as its military and political chief from 1827 and was raised to marshal and then Grand Marshal after Ayacucho; the navy, based at Guayaquil, was led by Commodore Thomas Charles. The other side was the Republic of Peru, independent of Spain since 1821 and capitaled at Lima, materially weaker than its opponent in both men and money. After President Jose de la Riva-Aguero was overthrown by the army in January 1827 and exiled to Europe, Peru was run by a legislature and a supreme military committee; a constituent congress met in June 1828, the Army of the North was handed to General Jose de La Mar with full powers, the fleet was under Admiral Martin, and the surviving royalist troops were led by Pezuela, appointed Grand Marshal and put at the disposal of the government. In June 1829 La Mar overturned the central government, set up a separate Grand Marshal of Peru regime in the south and turned the war into a three-way conflict that exhausted every party to it.
people: 核心人物是西蒙·波利瓦爾。他以解放者的身分率領大哥倫比亞的軍隊，先於一八二七年十二月在米拉河谷平定基多方面的叛亂，首領何塞·馬里亞·奧恩塔內達中重傷不治；其後他把主力投入對秘魯的戰爭。一八二八年二月二十七日，他與蘇克雷在塔爾基（又稱博塔丘埃洛）擊敗拉馬爾的北方軍，卻不顧傷亡與後方空虛執意越境追擊，同年十二月五日在 Ingaví 一役慘敗。蘇克雷是此戰最有效率的將領：他在塔爾基以參謀長身分策劃反擊，一八二八年十二月九日在亞亞庫喬擊潰皇家派主力，扭轉了整個南美戰局；一八二九年率軍深入秘魯，六月攻下塞羅德帕斯科，七月二十三日再勝於 Ingaví，九月初占領利馬。秘魯方面的關鍵人物是何塞·德·拉·馬爾，這位原籍布宜諾斯艾利斯、曾隨解放軍作戰的將領一八二七年率軍北進並攻入瓜亞基爾，兵敗後不甘屈居人下，於一八二九年六月推翻中央政府另立政府，最終兵敗下野。此外在場或牽動全局的，還有流亡中的秘魯首任總統拉瓦·阿吉羅、一八二八年制憲會議選出的總統阿古斯丁·加馬拉、率領死亡軍團的基多工匠上校何塞·菲利克斯·瓦爾迪維索、海軍上將馬丁與托馬斯·查爾斯、皇家派大元帥佩蘇埃拉，以及隨後在南部山區舉起公社黨人旗幟的胡安·何塞·弗洛雷斯與比森特·羅卡富埃。
peopleEn: The central figure was Simon Bolivar. As the Liberator he commanded the Gran Colombian army, first suppressing the rebellion in the Quito region at the Battle of Mira in December 1827, where the rebel chief Jose Maria Saenz de Ontaneda was fatally wounded, and then committing his main force to the war against Peru. On 27 February 1828 he and Sucre defeated La Mar's Army of the North at Tarqui, also called Portachuelo, but in defiance of his losses and of the empty country behind him he pressed the pursuit across the border and was badly beaten at Ingavi on 5 December 1828. Sucre was the most effective commander of the war: as chief of staff at Tarqui he planned the counterstroke, and on 9 December 1828 at Ayacucho he destroyed the main royalist army and turned the whole southern campaign. In 1829 he drove deep into Peru, took Cerro de Pasco in June, won again at Ingavi on 23 July and occupied Lima in early September. The decisive personality on the Peruvian side was Jose de La Mar, a Buenos Aires-born officer who had served with the patriots, led the northern invasion of 1827 into Guayaquil and, unwilling to serve under others after his defeat, overthrew the central government in June 1829 to found his own regime, only to be beaten and removed in turn. Others who mattered were the exiled first president of Peru Jose de la Riva-Aguero, the president elected by the constituent congress of 1828 Agustin Gamarra, the Quito guild colonel Jose Felix Valdivieso who commanded the Legion of Death, Admiral Martin and Commodore Thomas Charles at sea, the royalist Grand Marshal Pezuela, and Juan Jose Flores and Vicente Rocafuerte, who soon raised the communero flag in the southern mountains.
kits: 卡面這件輪發手槍是十六世紀初的西班牙產物：它以發條的扭力帶動擊錘撞擊燧石並同時帶動機構完成上膛，是最早的後膛手槍，機械結構昂貴，只有火槍隊的軍官與近衛才有資格配發。到一八二八年的戰場上，這種後膛機關槍早已退出現役，真正配發的是燧發手槍與燧發步槍；但輪發手槍確立的制度延續未改：手槍等同軍官身分，哥倫比亞與秘魯的團營以上軍官隨身佩帶手槍，用於警衛與近身自衛，而非作戰主力。步兵的骨幹是滑膛燧發步槍與卡賓槍，騎兵配卡賓槍加刺刀，並有以長矛配槍的長槍騎兵，正是長矛讓秘魯國民軍在亞亞庫喬頂住了皇家派密集的槍騎兵衝鋒。炮兵每連配四至六門四磅、六磅與八磅長管炮，另有十二磅攻城炮，攻壘與攻城任務由輕裝分遣隊擔任；工兵以柳條柴束築胸牆、用斧鏟修削坡面。畜力是真正的限制：安第斯山道只靠騾子馱運，一門炮連同彈藥要數十頭騾子分批拖行，山地行軍往往一日不足十公里。秘魯省區民兵中仍殘存火繩槍，基多工匠與部分志願兵使用獵槍。總之，輪發手槍在這場戰爭的位置，是已經退場的祖制：軍官佩著它所代表的權威，而不是靠它取勝。
kitsEn: The wheellock pistol on the card face is a sixteenth-century Spanish product: its mainspring drives a striker against the flint and, at the same time, works the mechanism that loads the weapon, making it the earliest breech-loading pistol. The mechanism was too costly to be common, and it was issued only to officers of the musket companies and to the guard. On the battlefields of 1828 the type had long since left active service; what troops actually carried were flintlock pistols and flintlock muskets. Yet the institution the wheellock had established survived intact, namely that the pistol was the badge of an officer: in both the Colombian and Peruvian armies officers down to battalion and company level wore a pistol for guard duty and personal defence rather than as a primary weapon. The backbone of the infantry was the smoothbore flintlock musket and the carbine; cavalrymen carried carbines with bayonets, and there were lancers armed with the lance and gun, and it was the lance that let the Peruvian national army absorb the massed lancer charges of the royalists at Ayacucho. Artillery batteries carried four to six guns of 4, 6 and 8 pounds, with 12-pounder siege pieces available, and light detachments handled assault and siege work. Engineers built breastworks from wicker fascines and cut firing steps with picks and shovels. Animal power was the real constraint: on Andean tracks everything travelled by mule, and a gun with its ammunition needed several dozen mules moved in stages, while a day's march rarely exceeded ten kilometres. Matchlock muskets still survived in Peruvian provincial levies, and the Quito artisans and some volunteers used hunting rifles. In short, the wheellock's place in this war was that of an obsolete institution: officers wore it for the authority it stood for, not to win battles.
tactics: 雙方都沿用拿破崙時代的戰術：步兵營以縱隊行軍，戰鬥中排成兩列縱隊前進，槍兵在三列射擊線後方齊射，關鍵時刻以刺刀線反推掩護；炮兵集中配在兩翼高地，騎兵在翼側待機實施衝鋒與追擊。哥倫比亞軍最核心的原則是佔領高地：先以獵兵與輕步兵驅散守軍，再以縱隊強攻山脊，迫使對手在仰角進攻中耗盡銳氣；亞亞庫喬正是以四個師的縱隊輪番強攻羅馬山莊一帶的幾處山頭，皇家派在正午烈日下仰攻而消耗殆盡。蘇克雷又把Junín輕騎兵改作散兵，用獵槍沿斜面射擊皇家派的槍騎兵，化解其衝鋒壓力。秘魯軍的對策是集中兵力與地理縱深：拉馬爾在北方利用高原隘口、村落堡壘與堅守遲滯哥倫比亞軍；一八二九年七月卻在 Ingaví 將三個師收攏成一次密集突擊，企圖一舉摧毀糖嶺上的蘇克雷主力，因兩翼警戒與火力配置失衡而崩潰。海上是封鎖與奪取制海權的角力，哥倫比亞分隊以快船封鎖瓜亞基爾，秘魯海軍則企圖切斷對方的海岸補給。補給線是決定性弱點：由基多南下要翻越安第斯山，雨季（十二月至五月）行軍艱苦，乾燥季（六月至九月）才利於遠征與大部隊作戰。
tacticsEn: Both sides fought with Napoleonic doctrine: infantry battalions marched in column and went into action in two ranks, musketeers firing in a three-line shooting order, bayonets used to push forward when the firing line faltered; artillery was massed on the flanks and on rising ground, and cavalry waited on the wings to charge and to pursue. The core principle of the Colombian army was to take the heights: light troops and skirmishers first drove the defenders off, then columns assaulted the ridge so that the enemy was spent attacking uphill. At Ayacucho this took the form of four divisions attacking in turn the positions around Cerro de la Punta, and the royalists were worn out climbing under the noon sun. Sucre even converted the Junin hussars into skirmishers, using hunting rifles to shoot down the slope at royalist lancers and break the weight of their charges. Peru's answer was concentration and geographical depth: in the north La Mar used highland defiles, village strongpoints and a stubborn defence to slow the Colombians down; in July 1829 he concentrated three divisions into a single dense attack at Ingavi with the intention of destroying Sucre's main body on the ridge of El Pan de Azúcar, and it collapsed because the flanks were poorly watched and the fire badly distributed. At sea the contest was between a blockade aimed at Guayaquil by fast Colombian vessels and a Peruvian effort to recover command of the coast. Supply was the decisive weakness: marching south from Quito meant crossing the Andes, the rainy season from December to May made movement gruelling, and only the dry season from June to September suited a long march and a major operation.
data: 兵力與損失的數字各來源記載不一，只能取其量級。一八二八年二月的塔爾基戰役，哥倫比亞方面出動約二千至二千五百人，秘魯北方軍約三千至四千人；哥倫比亞方傷亡數百，多數不是陣亡而是高山地區的嚴寒、勞累與高山症所致，秘魯軍雖敗卻撤退有緒，多數帶走火炮與輜重。亞亞庫喬一役，蘇克雷可用兵力約五千八百至六千，維多利亞何塞·德·拉·塞爾納的皇家派軍約一萬三千（實際投入戰鬥者略少），另有自上方高地出兵的縱隊；皇家派傷亡與被俘合計逾兩千人，數百人在撤退途中投降，其餘潰散，維多利亞於同日簽署投降書。一八二九年七月的 Ingaví，蘇克雷兵力約五千至六千，秘魯師約三千，被包圍後多數放下武器。地理數據上，基多至昆卡約三百公里，基多至亞亞庫喬約七百至九百公里。財政上，哥倫比亞一八二二年在倫敦籌得約四百二十萬英鎊貸款，是這場戰爭的直接軍費來源，秘魯則因稅源與信用不足而難以長期養兵。國力對比上，秘魯人口約二百萬，哥倫比亞聯邦連同委內瑞拉與新格拉納達合計約六百萬，人均資源差距進一步拉大雙方在補給與糧秣上的落差。
dataEn: Figures for strengths and losses differ from source to source, so only the order of magnitude can be given. At the Battle of Tarqui in February 1828 the Colombians fielded perhaps 2,000 to 2,500 men against three to four thousand in the Peruvian Army of the North; Colombian casualties ran to several hundred, most of them from cold, exhaustion and altitude sickness in the high country rather than from enemy fire, while the defeated Peruvians withdrew in good order carrying most of their guns and baggage. At Ayacucho Sucre had about 5,800 to 6,000 men available against roughly 13,000 under the viceroy Jose de la Serna, fewer of whom actually took part, with additional columns descending from the heights above; royalist dead and captured exceeded two thousand, several hundred more surrendered during the retreat, and the rest broke up, the viceroy signing the capitulation the same day. At Ingavi in July 1829 Sucre numbered about 5,000 to 6,000 against roughly three thousand Peruvians, most of whom laid down their arms once surrounded. On distances, Quito to Cuenca is about 300 kilometres and Quito to Ayacucho some 700 to 900. On finance, the London loan of 1822 raised roughly 4.2 million pounds for Colombia and was the direct source of war funding for this conflict, while Peru, short of tax revenue and credit, could not sustain an army in the field. On weight of population, Peru had some two million inhabitants against perhaps six million for the Colombian federation including Venezuela and New Granada, and the gap in per-capita resources widened the difference between the two sides in supply and rations.
cause: 打起來的原因有四層。第一是舊有的邊界糾紛：秘魯與基多之間的高地界線從未被清楚勘定，秘魯方面堅持恢復西班牙時期總督區的傳統版圖，把基多、瓜亞基爾與南部山區都視為自己的勢力範圍。第二是秘魯北部的政治崩潰：一八二七年總統拉瓦·阿吉羅被推翻、北軍節節失利，讓利馬感到整個北部即將淪陷，拉馬爾遂率軍越過阿卡山谷攻入基多。第三是哥倫比亞的戰略目標：波利瓦爾自一八二四年起就打算解放秘魯，奪取鹽礦與火藥物資，把整個南部邊界一次性解決，他在塔爾基取勝後不肯停手，就是要一舉摧毀秘魯軍。第四是基多地區本身的叛亂：一八二六年起以弗洛雷斯與羅卡富埃為首的公社黨人在南部山區鼓動，奧恩塔內達另立厄瓜多爾國並懸掛藍白藍旗，使基多一度脫離聯邦，哥倫比亞必須先平叛再南下。財政同樣是導火線：兩國的英債都被用來購買軍火與維持軍餉，都沒有餘力長期養兵，速戰速決的訴求反而推高了戰爭烈度。
causeEn: There were four layers of cause behind the fighting. First, an old boundary dispute: the highland frontier between Peru and Quito had never been properly surveyed, and Peru held to the traditional limits of the Spanish viceroyalties, treating Quito, Guayaquil and the southern mountains as its own sphere. Second, the political collapse of northern Peru: after the overthrow of President Riva-Aguero in 1827 and a series of defeats in the north, Lima feared the loss of the whole northern half of the country, and La Mar marched across the mountains into Quito accordingly. Third, Colombian war aims: from 1824 onwards Bolivar had intended the liberation of Peru, the seizure of saltpetre and gunpowder, and a final settlement of the southern frontier, and his refusal to stop after Tarqui was meant to destroy the Peruvian army in one stroke. Fourth, a rebellion inside the Quito region itself: from 1826 the communeros led by Flores and Rocafuerte stirred the southern mountains, and Ontaneda proclaimed a separate state of Ecuador with its own blue-and-white flag, so the Colombian government had to suppress the revolt before it could march south. Finance was a fuse as well: British credit on both sides was spent on arms and pay, neither treasury could carry an army for long, and the pressure for quick decisions raised the intensity of the war.
impact: 這場戰爭的歷史後果遠大於它本身的邊界收益。一八二八年十二月九日的亞亞庫喬是西班牙美洲獨立戰爭的最後一場決定會戰，維多利亞於同日簽署投降書，西班牙在南美洲的殖民統治就此終結；但秘魯與哥倫比亞的邊界衝突並未隨西班牙王位空缺而收束，反而在真空下更形尖銳。亞亞庫喬的勝利同時把大哥倫比亞推向財政與內政的極限：一八二九年底波利瓦爾交出軍權，一八三〇年聯邦解體，基多省獨立成為厄瓜多爾，秘魯與厄瓜多爾的邊界爭端從一八三一年蘇耶人戰爭、一八五七至一八五八年戰爭到今日的赤道線與安第斯水源爭議，都可視為本場衝突的直接延伸。戰術層面，佔領高地與散兵滲透的組合在亞亞庫喬成熟，隨後被玻利維亞與秘魯在一八三六至一八三九年戰爭中反覆運用；拉馬爾另立政府則分裂了秘魯國家本身，說明勝方在勝利的當年也無法整合整個安第斯山區。此外，哥倫比亞聯邦一八二二年的英債最終由後繼的哥倫比亞與厄瓜多爾在十九世紀中葉以新一輪英債清償，成為這場戰爭留給後人最昂貴的帳單。
impactEn: The historical consequences of this war far outstripped its territorial gains. The Battle of Ayacucho on 9 December 1828 was the last decisive engagement of the Spanish American wars of independence: the viceroy signed the capitulation the same day and Spanish rule in South America was over. The border conflict between Peru and Colombia, however, did not settle with the Spanish crown's departure; it sharpened in the vacuum that followed. The victory at Ayacucho also pushed Gran Colombia to the limit of its finances and its domestic politics: Bolivar gave up command in late 1829, the federation broke up in 1830, and the former Quito department became the independent state of Ecuador. The Peru-Ecuador frontier dispute, from the War of the Suyes in 1831 and the war of 1857 to 1858 down to present-day arguments over the equator line and Andean water rights, can be read as a direct extension of this conflict. Tactically, the combination of seizing the heights with skirmisher infiltration matured at Ayacucho and was repeatedly used again in the war between Bolivia and Peru from 1836 to 1839. La Mar's separatist regime, meanwhile, split Peru itself, showing that even the victor in 1828 could not integrate the Andean highlands. And the British loan of 1822 contracted by the Colombian federation was eventually repaid by its successors, Colombia and Ecuador, through new British borrowing in the middle of the nineteenth century: the most expensive bill this war left behind.
result: 軍事上的結局清楚：塔爾基（一八二八年二月二十七日）由哥倫比亞取勝，Ingaví（一八二八年十二月五日）波利瓦爾本人失利，亞亞庫喬（一八二八年十二月九日）蘇克雷大破皇家派，一八二九年四月塞羅德帕斯科、七月 Ingaví，蘇克雷再度擊敗秘魯軍並於八月占領利馬。政治上，雙方都沒有能力把對方從地圖上抹去：一八二九年九月底蘇克雷與秘魯代表在瓜亞基爾達成協議，以大戰前的實際控制線為準，秘魯保住北部高原與利馬，基多保住南部山區與瓜亞基爾港口，爭議地帶留待往後商定；此後拉馬爾在南部的分裂政權與利馬政府內鬥，一八三〇年拉馬爾下野並在赴任途中被舊僕殺害，秘魯重新統一，而大哥倫比亞亦於一八三〇年解體，蘇克雷掌管的北方軍與本土派因權力安排與秘魯戰事的牽扯而分道揚鑣。一八三四至一八三五年哥倫比亞聯邦與秘魯及玻利維亞同盟再起衝突，蘇克雷在一八三五年八月二十五日的貝魯埃科斯戰役中陣亡，成為這場戰爭最令人惋惜的餘波。
resultEn: The military outcome is clear. Tarqui on 27 February 1828 went to Colombia; Bolivar himself was defeated at Ingavi on 5 December 1828; Sucre shattered the royalist army at Ayacucho on 9 December 1828; and in 1829 came Cerro de Pasco in April and Ingavi in July, after which Sucre again beat the Peruvian army and occupied Lima in August. Politically, neither side could erase the other from the map. At the end of September 1829 Sucre's representatives reached an agreement at Guayaquil that took the pre-war line of actual control as the basis: Peru kept the northern highlands and Lima, Quito kept the southern mountains and the port of Guayaquil, and the disputed zone was left for later negotiation. La Mar's separatist regime in the south then fought the Lima government from within; in 1830 La Mar fell and was killed on his journey by a former servant, and Peru was reunited, while Gran Colombia itself dissolved in 1830, with Sucre's northern army and the metropolitan faction in Bogotá parting ways over the settlement of power and the wars in Peru. Renewed fighting between the Colombian federation and the Peru-Bolivia confederation in 1834 and 1835 ended with Sucre's death at the Battle of Berruecos on 25 August 1835, the saddest epilogue of the whole war.
